exercise.name: Dumbbell Alternate V-up

reference.title: Dumbbell Alternate V up
reference.listing: Video; the page could not be read here (blocked), so the movement follows the name and standard coaching (V-up raising one leg at a time, dumbbell held in both hands).

exercise.mechanics: Compound (trunk flexion with single-leg hip flexion)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you fold up, in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, short hold, about 1.6 s down per side

prescription.tempo: Controlled; no bouncing off the mat
prescription.progression: Slower lowering, then a heavier dumbbell, then the full V-up with both legs

cues.text: Lie on your back, legs long. Hold one dumbbell by its ends overhead, arms long, just off the mat.
Fold up: lift the trunk and the straight right leg together and reach the dumbbell toward the right shin.
Pause: back of the pelvis on the mat, left leg long on the floor.
Lower the trunk and leg slowly to the mat, arms back overhead.
Now the left leg: fold up and reach toward the left shin.
Lower under control to the start.

mistakes.mistake: Swinging the arms and dumbbell to throw the trunk up
mistakes.fix: Lift with the abdominals; the arms follow.
Keep it straight; lift only as high as you can with a straight leg.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the dumbbell crash into the mat overhead
mistakes.fix: Lower it under control and stop just above the mat.

mistakes.mistake: Lower back arching off the mat as the legs lower

kinematics.measure: Trunk (pelvis to C7) from the floor
kinematics.norm: Trunk raised toward the leg; V-up style exercises drew high rectus abdominis and oblique activity (Escamilla 2006)
One leg raised, the other long on the mat (standard coaching)
Hip flexors are strongly active when the legs are raised and the trunk lifts (Andersson 1997)
Long, dumbbell overhead to above the shin (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #16927, Dumbbell Alternate V up, video (movement reference)
Escamilla et al. 2006, electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises (Phys Ther 86(5):656-671)
Andersson, Nilsson, Ma and Thorstensson 1997, abdominal and hip flexor muscle activation during various training exercises (Eur J Appl Physiol 75:115-123; PMID 9118976)
Axler and McGill 1997, low-back loads over a variety of abdominal exercises: searching for the safest abdominal challenge (Med Sci Sports Exerc 29(6):804-811)

cautions: Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Low-back pain or a disc problem: repeated loaded trunk flexion may aggravate it; try a dead bug instead (Axler and McGill 1997).
Hold the dumbbell firmly by both ends and keep it off the face.
Diastasis recti or pregnancy: ask a clinician before doing V-ups.
modify: Smaller range: shoulders only off the mat.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis curls the trunk up toward the leg; V-up style exercises showed high abdominal activity in Escamilla 2006.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Lift the straight leg and help fold the trunk up (Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Lift the straight leg and help fold the trunk up (Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Help the curl and the slight turn toward the raised leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Help the curl and the slight turn toward the raised leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Rectus femoris keeps the raised knee straight and helps lift the leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Rectus femoris keeps the raised knee straight and helps lift the leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the dumbbell up with long arms (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the dumbbell up with long arms (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Reaches the shoulder blades forward (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Reaches the shoulder blades forward (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Press the hands into the dumbbell ends (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Press the hands into the dumbbell ends (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Keep the legs in line (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Keep the legs in line (clinical opinion).
